source.text: שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹתאֵ֭לֶיךָ נָשָׂ֣אתִי אֶת־עֵינַ֑י הַ֝יֹּשְׁבִ֗י בַּשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: The song of the ascents. To you I have lifted up my eyes, the [one] sitting in the heavens.

en.L: A song of ascents. To {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} I lift up my eyes, [the one] sitting in the heavens.
en.B: A song of ascents. I raise my eyes to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, the one who reigns in heaven.
en.R: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem. I look up to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You sit on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} throne in heaven.

fr.L: Cantique des montées. Vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} je lève mes yeux, [{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui] sièges dans les cieux.
fr.B: Cantique des montées. Je lève les yeux vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, qui règnes dans les cieux.
fr.R: Chant pour la montée vers Jérusalem. Je lève les yeux vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. Tu es assis sur {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} trône dans le ciel.

sw.L: Wimbo wa kupanda. Kwako ninainua macho yangu, ewe uketiye mbinguni.
sw.B: Wimbo wa kupanda. Ninainua macho yangu kukutazama {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}, unayetawala mbinguni.
sw.R: Wimbo wa safari ya kupanda kwenda Yerusalemu. Ninakutazama {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}}. Umeketi katika kiti {{deity_pronoun:chako|Chako}} cha enzi mbinguni.

es.L: Cántico de las subidas. Hacia {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} alzo mis ojos, [el que] está sentado en los cielos.
es.B: Cántico de las subidas. Levanto mis ojos hacia {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, el que reina en el cielo.
es.R: Canto para el viaje de subida a Jerusalén. Miro hacia {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. Tú estás sentado en {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} trono en el cielo.

vi.L: Bài ca cho những lần đi lên. Tôi ngước mắt lên cùng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, [Đấng] ngự trên các tầng trời.
vi.B: Bài ca đi lên. Tôi ngước mắt nhìn lên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, là Đấng ngự trị trên trời.
vi.R: Bài ca cho cuộc hành trình lên Giê-ru-sa-lem. Tôi ngước nhìn lên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Ngài ngồi trên ngai của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ở trên trời.

ko.L: 올라감을 위한 노래. 주님께 제가 제 눈을 듭니다, 하늘에 앉아 계신 분이시여.
ko.B: 올라가며 부르는 노래. 하늘에서 다스리시는 주님, 제가 주님께 눈을 듭니다.
ko.R: 예루살렘으로 올라가며 부르는 노래. 제가 주님을 올려다봅니다. 주님께서는 하늘에서 보좌에 앉아 계십니다.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: As in 120:1, the short title and the first line are counted together as verse 1, so the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: a song of ascents: probably a pilgrim song
decisions.reason: As in 120:1: one of the fifteen songs probably sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: sitting: sitting enthroned
decisions.reason: The verb (yashav) used of God means sitting as king on his throne (2:4; 29:10).

decisions.choice: I have lifted up: I lift up now
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form often used for past events, but here it describes what the psalmist is doing now.

decisions.choice: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As in 120:1.

decisions.choice: reigns (B); sit on your throne (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what God's sitting means (m3).

decisions.choice: "Ngài" for "you" as the singer speaks to God
decisions.reason: As in the published Psalms 23 and 139, the psalmist speaks to God as "Ngài", with the deity_pronoun setting the English has.

decisions.choice: The prayer to God is in 합쇼체 with "저/제"; the Hebrew "you" is the title "주님", with no span
decisions.reason: Style guide section 7a. Korean addresses God by title rather than a pronoun; "주님" here is not the divine name, so it carries no divine_name span.

source.text: הִנֵּ֨ה כְעֵינֵ֪י עֲבָדִ֡ים אֶל־יַ֤ד אֲֽדוֹנֵיהֶ֗ם כְּעֵינֵ֣י שִׁפְחָה֮ אֶל־יַ֪ד גְּבִ֫רְתָּ֥הּ כֵּ֣ן עֵ֭ינֵינוּ אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ עַ֝֗ד שֶׁיְּחָנֵּֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, as [the] eyes of slaves to [the] hand of their masters, as [the] eyes of a female slave to [the] hand of her mistress, so our eyes [are] to YHWH our God until that he shows us favor.

en.L: Look, as the eyes of slaves [are] to the hand of their masters, as the eyes of a female slave [are] to the hand of her mistress, so our eyes [are] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God until {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} shows us favor.
en.B: Servants watch the hand of their master, and a servant woman watches the hand of the woman she serves. In the same way we keep our eyes on {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God, waiting for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to show us favor.
en.R: Servants keep watching their master's hand to see what he wants or what he will give. A servant woman watches the hand of the woman she works for. In the same way, we keep looking to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. We wait for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to be kind to us.

fr.L: Voici, comme les yeux des esclaves [sont] vers la main de leurs maîtres, comme les yeux d’une esclave [sont] vers la main de sa maîtresse, ainsi nos yeux [sont] vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu, jusqu’à ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous fasse grâce.
fr.B: Les serviteurs regardent la main de leur maître, et la servante regarde la main de sa maîtresse. De même, nous gardons les yeux fixés sur {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu, en attendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nous fasse grâce.
fr.R: Les serviteurs regardent sans cesse la main de leur maître pour voir ce qu’il veut ou ce qu’il va leur donner. La servante regarde la main de la femme pour qui elle travaille. De même, nous ne quittons pas des yeux {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} notre Dieu. Nous attendons qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} soit bon pour nous.

sw.L: Tazama, kama macho ya watumwa [yalivyo] kwa mkono wa mabwana wao, kama macho ya mjakazi [yalivyo] kwa mkono wa bibi yake, ndivyo macho yetu [yalivyo] kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu mpaka atakapotuhurumia.
sw.B: Watumishi huutazama mkono wa bwana wao, na mtumishi wa kike huutazama mkono wa bibi anayemtumikia. Vivyo hivyo tunaendelea kumtazama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu, tukimngoja atuhurumie.
sw.R: Watumishi huendelea kuutazama mkono wa bwana wao ili waone anachotaka au atakachowapa. Mtumishi wa kike huutazama mkono wa bibi anayemfanyia kazi. Vivyo hivyo, sisi tunaendelea kumtazama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wetu. Tunamngoja atuonee wema.

es.L: Mira, como los ojos de los esclavos [están puestos] en la mano de sus señores, como los ojos de la esclava [están puestos] en la mano de su señora, así nuestros ojos [están puestos] en {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios, hasta que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos muestre su favor.
es.B: Los siervos observan la mano de su señor, y la sierva observa la mano de la mujer a quien sirve. Así también nosotros tenemos los ojos puestos en {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} nuestro Dios, esperando que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} nos muestre su favor.
es.R: Los siervos no dejan de mirar la mano de su amo para ver qué quiere o qué les va a dar. La sierva mira la mano de la mujer para quien trabaja. Así también nosotros seguimos mirando {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} nuestro Dios. Esperamos que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} sea bondadoso con nosotros.

vi.L: Này, như mắt của những nô lệ [hướng] về tay của chủ mình, như mắt của nữ nô lệ [hướng] về tay của bà chủ mình, thì mắt chúng tôi [hướng] về {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời chúng tôi, cho đến khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tỏ ơn cho chúng tôi.
vi.B: Đầy tớ dõi theo tay của chủ mình, và người tớ gái dõi theo tay của bà chủ mình. Cũng vậy, mắt chúng tôi hướng về {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời chúng tôi, chờ đợi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tỏ ơn cho chúng tôi.
vi.R: Đầy tớ cứ nhìn theo tay của chủ mình, để xem chủ muốn gì hay sẽ cho gì. Người tớ gái nhìn theo tay của bà chủ mình. Cũng vậy, chúng tôi cứ trông lên {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đức Chúa Trời chúng tôi. Chúng tôi chờ đợi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tỏ lòng thương xót chúng tôi.

ko.L: 보아라, 종들의 눈이 그들 주인의 손을 [향하듯], 여종의 눈이 그 여주인의 손을 [향하듯], 우리 눈이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 우리 하나님을 [향하니], 그분께서 우리에게 은혜를 베푸실 때까지이다.
ko.B: 종들은 주인의 손을 지켜보고, 여종은 자기가 섬기는 여주인의 손을 지켜본다. 그처럼 우리도 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 우리 하나님께 눈을 두고, 그분께서 우리에게 은혜를 베풀어 주시기를 기다린다.
ko.R: 종들은 주인이 무엇을 원하는지, 무엇을 줄지 알려고 주인의 손을 계속 지켜본다. 여종은 자기가 일하는 집 여주인의 손을 지켜본다. 그처럼 우리도 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 우리 하나님을 계속 바라본다. 그분께서 우리에게 친절을 베푸시기를 기다린다.

decisions.choice: the hand of their master: signal and gift
decisions.reason: Slaves watched the master's hand for a sign of what was wanted, for the food and wages it handed out, and for help. The picture is of complete attention and dependence.

decisions.choice: show favor: be gracious
decisions.reason: The verb (chanan) means to show undeserved kindness to someone in need. It is repeated twice in verse 3.

decisions.choice: masters: plural of majesty or each one's master
decisions.reason: The word for "their master" is plural in form, as it often is for a master or lord; it may also mean each slave's own master.

decisions.choice: to see what he wants or what he will give
decisions.reason: Readable explains why the servants watch the hand (m1).

decisions.choice: servants; servant woman
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that these are slaves watching a master, and Literal keeps "slaves" and "female slave".

decisions.choice: "esclaves", "une esclave" (Literal); "serviteurs", "la servante" (Balanced, Readable) for ʿavadim and shifḥah
decisions.reason: As the French terms set for ʿeved: "esclave" at Literal, "serviteur" at Balanced and Readable, as the English does. The feminine shifḥah follows the same pattern.

decisions.choice: "kuhurumia" (L, B) for showing favor; "kuonea wema" (be kind to) at Readable
decisions.reason: The Hebrew asks God to be gracious. "Kuhurumia" is the everyday word for showing undeserved kindness to someone in need; "fadhili" is kept for the Hebrew hesed (loyal love) in these psalms, so it is not used here.

decisions.choice: esclavos, esclava (L); siervos, sierva (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew 'eved and shifchah are slaves. Literal says "esclavos" and "esclava"; Balanced and Readable say "siervos" and "sierva", as the English says "servants", following the book-wide choice for 'eved.

decisions.choice: "nô lệ", "nữ nô lệ" (L); "đầy tớ", "người tớ gái" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the one for a slave, and Literal keeps that; Balanced and Readable say "servant" for people who wait on their master's hand, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Verse 2 speaks about the LORD in the plain written style with the honorific, between the prayers of verses 1 and 3
alternatives: 합쇼체 with 저희 throughout the psalm
decisions.reason: The verse names "the LORD our God" and "he" in the third person, so it is speech about God (style guide section 7a); verses 1, 3 and 4 speak to him.

source.text: חָנֵּ֣נוּ יְהוָ֣ה חָנֵּ֑נוּ כִּֽי־רַ֝֗ב שָׂבַ֥עְנוּ בֽוּז׃

records.literal_gloss: Show us favor, YHWH, show us favor, for much we have been filled [with] contempt.

en.L: Show us favor, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, show us favor, for we have been greatly filled [with] contempt.
en.B: Show us favor, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, show us favor, for we have swallowed more contempt than we can bear.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, be kind to us! Be kind to us! People have looked down on us more than we can stand.

fr.L: Fais-nous grâce, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, fais-nous grâce, car nous avons été grandement rassasiés de mépris.
fr.B: Fais-nous grâce, {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, fais-nous grâce, car nous avons avalé plus de mépris que nous n’en pouvons supporter.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, sois bon pour nous ! Sois bon pour nous ! Les gens nous ont méprisés plus que nous ne pouvons le supporter.

sw.L: Utuhurumie, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, utuhurumie, kwa maana tumeshibishwa sana dharau.
sw.B: Utuhurumie, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, utuhurumie, kwa maana tumemeza dharau kuliko tunavyoweza kustahimili.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, utuonee wema! Utuonee wema! Watu wametudharau kuliko tunavyoweza kuvumilia.

es.L: Muéstranos tu favor, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, muéstranos tu favor, porque estamos muy hartos [de] desprecio.
es.B: Muéstranos tu favor, {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, muéstranos tu favor, porque hemos tragado más desprecio del que podemos soportar.
es.R: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¡sé bondadoso con nosotros! ¡Sé bondadoso con nosotros! La gente nos ha despreciado más de lo que podemos aguantar.

vi.L: Xin tỏ ơn cho chúng tôi, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin tỏ ơn cho chúng tôi, vì chúng tôi đã bị no nê sự khinh miệt quá nhiều.
vi.B: Xin tỏ ơn cho chúng tôi, lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin tỏ ơn cho chúng tôi, vì chúng tôi đã phải nuốt sự khinh miệt nhiều hơn sức mình chịu nổi.
vi.R: Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, xin thương xót chúng tôi! Xin thương xót chúng tôi! Người ta đã khinh dể chúng tôi đến mức chúng tôi không chịu nổi nữa.

ko.L: 저희에게 은혜를 베풀어 주십시오, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 저희에게 은혜를 베풀어 주십시오. 저희가 멸시로 너무나 배불러졌습니다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 은혜를 베풀어 주십시오. 저희에게 은혜를 베풀어 주십시오. 저희는 견딜 수 없을 만큼 멸시를 삼켰습니다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 저희에게 친절을 베풀어 주십시오! 저희에게 친절을 베풀어 주십시오! 사람들이 저희를 견딜 수 없을 만큼 업신여겼습니다.

decisions.choice: filled with contempt: had too much of it
decisions.reason: To be "filled" or "sated" with something is to have had more than enough of it. Here the people have been made to swallow contempt until they can take no more.

decisions.choice: contempt: being despised
decisions.reason: The word (buz) is scorn shown to people treated as worthless (Nehemiah 3:36 has the same complaint).

decisions.choice: People have looked down on us
decisions.reason: Readable says who showed contempt and what it was.

decisions.choice: "저희" for "us" in prayer
decisions.reason: "저희" is the humble form of "우리" that Korean uses when a group speaks to a superior; it goes with "저" and 합쇼체.

source.text: רַבַּת֮ שָֽׂבְעָה־לָּ֪הּ נַ֫פְשֵׁ֥נוּ הַלַּ֥עַג הַשַּׁאֲנַנִּ֑ים הַ֝בּ֗וּז לִגְאֵ֥יוֹנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Much has it been filled for itself, our soul, [with] the mockery of the ones at ease, the contempt of the proud.

en.L: Our soul has been greatly filled for itself [with] the mockery of those at ease, the contempt of the proud.
en.B: We have had our fill and more of the mockery of the comfortable and the contempt of the arrogant.
en.R: We are tired of being mocked by people with easy lives, and of being looked down on by proud people.

fr.L: Notre âme a été grandement rassasiée pour elle-même de la moquerie de ceux qui sont tranquilles, du mépris des orgueilleux.
fr.B: Nous en avons plus qu’assez de la moquerie des gens satisfaits et du mépris des arrogants.
fr.R: Nous sommes fatigués que des gens à la vie facile se moquent de nous, et que des orgueilleux nous regardent de haut.

sw.L: Nafsi yetu imeshibishwa sana dhihaka ya wale wanaostarehe, dharau ya wenye kiburi.
sw.B: Tumeshiba na kupita kiasi dhihaka ya watu wanaoishi kwa raha na dharau ya wenye majivuno.
sw.R: Tumechoka kudhihakiwa na watu wenye maisha ya raha, na kudharauliwa na watu wenye kiburi.

es.L: Muy harta está nuestra alma de la burla de los que viven tranquilos, del desprecio de los soberbios.
es.B: Ya estamos más que hartos de la burla de los que viven cómodos y del desprecio de los arrogantes.
es.R: Estamos cansados de que se burle de nosotros la gente que vive sin problemas, y de que nos desprecie la gente orgullosa.

vi.L: Linh hồn chúng tôi đã bị no nê quá nhiều sự chế nhạo của những kẻ an nhàn, sự khinh miệt của những kẻ kiêu ngạo.
vi.B: Chúng tôi đã chịu quá đủ sự chế nhạo của những kẻ sống an nhàn và sự khinh miệt của những kẻ kiêu căng.
vi.R: Chúng tôi đã mệt mỏi vì bị những kẻ sống sung sướng chế giễu, và bị những kẻ kiêu ngạo coi thường.

ko.L: 저희 영혼이 안일한 자들의 조롱과 교만한 자들의 멸시로 너무나 배불러졌습니다.
ko.B: 저희는 안락하게 사는 자들의 비웃음과 거만한 자들의 멸시를 넘치도록 받았습니다.
ko.R: 저희는 편하게 사는 사람들에게 놀림받는 것도, 교만한 사람들에게 무시당하는 것도 지쳤습니다.

decisions.choice: those at ease: the complacent
decisions.reason: The word (sha'anan) means untroubled and secure. Here it describes people comfortable enough to look down on others (Amos 6:1; Isaiah 32:9).

decisions.choice: much ... filled: repeated from verse 3
decisions.reason: The verse takes up the end of verse 3, "much ... filled", and says what the contempt was and who showed it.

decisions.choice: our soul (L); we (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Psalms 1-12, nefesh is "soul" at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "me" or "my life", since the word means the whole living person.
